blocks.text: The image presents a schematic diagram, likely from a physics or mathematics textbook, illustrating the concept of symmetry operations, specifically translations, on a rectangular grid. The diagram is divided into two sections. The top section features a large rectangle containing three black dots arranged in a vertical line: one at the top, one in the middle, and one at the bottom. Below this rectangle, three letters—A, B, and C—are aligned horizontally, indicating the three distinct translation vectors or symmetries applied to the grid. The bottom section displays four vertically oriented rectangles, each containing four black dots arranged in a 2x2 grid. These rectangles represent the result of applying the translations labeled A, B, and C to the original grid. Specifically, the dot positions in the bottom rectangles correspond to the original positions in the top rectangle: the top-left dot in the bottom rectangle is the original top dot, the top-right dot is the original middle dot, and the bottom-left and bottom-right dots are the original bottom dot. The diagram visually demonstrates how a 2D grid is transformed by shifting it along its own axes.
